title: R1: Add Stop-hook verification-evidence gate for completion claims
description:
Why: asd workflow mine flags validation-explicit-verify as the ONLY contradicted rule in the corpus (78 supporting / 2,092 contradicting sessions), while asd skill report verify-before-complete shows 0.98 adherence in the 1,676 sessions where the skill fires. Conclusion: the skill works when loaded but usually never engages; enforcement must move from skill-trigger to harness-structural.
What: a Stop hook (or PreToolUse gate on td review / git commit / gh pr create) that flags completion-shaped final messages (done / complete / it works / merged / tests pass) when the same turn lacks fresh command-output evidence.
Scope boundary: advisory (warn) mode only in this task; blocking mode is a separate future decision. Hook source canonical in ~/.hub, projected to runtime settings.
acceptance:
- Hook exists in ~/.hub canonical source and is installed into the Claude runtime settings projection.
- Fires on completion-shaped claims with no command evidence in the final turn; silent otherwise.
- Advisory mode; false-positive rate spot-checked against 10 recent real sessions and documented.
Verification: synthetic session with an unverified completion claim triggers the warning; a claim with fresh command evidence does not. After ~2 weeks, re-run 'asd workflow mine --json' and confirm contradicting_count for validation-explicit-verify is trending down; log the numbers on this task.

title: Close the distillery feedback loop (read-back + reinforcement)
Enforce audit-backed agent rules structurally in the harness
description:
Outcome: the most-violated or most-relearned agent rules from the 2026-07 asd session audit (9,421 sessions) stop relying on prose and become structural enforcement (hooks + contract text).
Evidence: validation-explicit-verify contradicted in 2,092 sessions vs 78 supporting (asd workflow mine); the run_in_background-for->300s lesson independently relearned in 3+ projects; scope-correction rule (2,265 supporting sessions, 0 contradictions) absent from contracts; tdd-guide is the #1 skill_ref (594) but has no installed SKILL.md; git skill adherence 0.80 across 3,374 sessions with a 74-item checklist.
Scope boundary: implementation surfaces live in ~/.hub (contracts, hook scripts) and ~/.claude runtime installs. This board tracks the work because the evidence and the re-measurement commands (asd workflow mine / asd skill report) live in this repo. Do not refactor unrelated contract sections or skills.

title: U6: trigger backfill for trigger-less instincts (budget-gated)
description: Extend LLM review-learnings with trigger reconstruction; cap reasoning effort per docs/solutions openrouter doc; serialize after td-683c75 sweep. Target trigger-less 78%->'<25%' on reprocessed.

title: R3: Add PreToolUse guard for long foreground commands without timeout
description:
Why: 29 timeout/long-command failure modes in the reviewed corpus, and the exact lesson 'use run_in_background=true for commands exceeding 300s' was independently re-derived in 3+ separate projects — prose in AGENTS.md is not preventing it.
What: a PreToolUse(Bash) hook that warns when a known-long command (codex exec, grok -p, cursor-agent --print, full builds, full test suites) is launched foreground without an explicit timeout (>=600000) or run_in_background.
Scope boundary: advisory warning only; maintain the known-long command list in one place in ~/.hub.
acceptance:
- Hook detects the documented known-long command list.
- Warns on foreground launch without explicit timeout/run_in_background; silent when either is present.
Verification: feed synthetic PreToolUse payloads (codex exec without timeout -> warn; with timeout: 600000 -> silent; grok -p backgrounded -> silent) and paste results into the task log.

title: R4: Restore tdd-guide skill surface (top skill_ref, not installed)
description:
Why: tdd-guide is the #1 skill referenced by reviewed learnings (594 skill_refs) but 'asd skill report tdd-guide' finds no SKILL.md in ~/.claude/skills, ~/.cursor/skills, or ~/.hub/artifacts/skills — it exists only as an agent definition. The demand signal says test-first guidance is the top skill need, and adherence cannot be measured for a skill that is not installed.
What: either install/ship a tdd-guide SKILL.md via the hub, or repoint the skill_ref extraction mapping with a documented decision.
Scope boundary: do not rewrite the tdd agent itself; this is about the skill surface / ref mapping only.
acceptance:
- 'asd skill report tdd-guide' returns an adherence report instead of 'not found', OR the skill_ref mapping decision is documented and reflected in extraction.
Verification: paste the skill report output (or the mapping diff) into the task log.

title: U12: Lift learning reachability from 25.6 percent
description:
Why: asd stats shows produced=2,206 but reachable=565 (25.6%), with only 175 of 414 projects having any reachable learnings — despite the read-back plumbing shipped in U1-U10. Distillation without read-back is inventory, not learning.
What: root-cause why ~74% of produced learnings are unreachable (un-rendered rollups? project-id mapping gaps? review backlog — see U11?), fix the dominant cause, re-measure.
Dependency note: partially coupled to U11 (review backlog) and U6 (trigger backfill, currently blocked) — investigate first, then declare the real dependency.
acceptance:
- Root-cause note logged with the dominant unreachability cause quantified.
- Fix implemented for the dominant cause, or follow-up tasks filed with ids.
- 'asd stats' reachable_ratio re-measured and improved; before/after numbers on this task.
Verification: paste before/after asd stats reachability block into the task log.

title: Unify pipeline, recall, and storage health for operators
description: Make the working product legible without requiring operators to interpret several JSON-heavy commands. Extend existing stats, pipeline gate, quality audit, doctor provider, recall telemetry, and static dashboard readers rather than adding another scanner or server.
acceptance: One human-readable command and the static dashboard answer: is the pipeline healthy, did recall deliver, is reviewed output fresh, what budget remains, is storage under pressure, and what should I do next; JSON output remains available; expensive filesystem counts are bounded or optional; fixture tests cover healthy, no-memory, stale-review, budget-blocked, recall-failure, and storage-pressure states; script/cibuild passes.

title: External staging storage
description: Import docs/plans/2026-07-18-feat-external-staging-storage-plan.md into td. Done means ASD can move parsed and reduced staging artifacts to a validated external staging root with fail-closed behavior, receipt-backed migration, and documented SSK cutover and rollback, while keeping any future S3 cold tier explicitly optional.
acceptance: Epic has child issues U1-U5 reflecting docs/plans/2026-07-18-feat-external-staging-storage-plan.md; U1 depends through U4 in order; U5 remains optional, P3, and blocked by U4; each unit records existing implementation surfaces for cold pickup.

title: H3: Surface shared health and recall delivery in the static dashboard
description: Render the same operator-health model in report --html, adding current status, degraded reasons, recall delivery/reachability, review freshness, storage pressure, and the recommended next action. Preserve the offline single-file architecture and eager-list/lazy-detail payload discipline.
acceptance: Dashboard health values match CLI JSON for the same fixture; client-rendered tests assert static copy plus embedded payload fields rather than assumed post-render HTML; eager payload remains bounded; live report generation completes on the current corpus; no new server or duplicate query path; script/cibuild passes.

title: U5: Optional S3 cold-tier offload and restore
description: Why: any S3 lane is optional, billable follow-on work that must remain outside the live local-filesystem contract. Done means an explicitly approved offload and restore lane can upload immutable, compressed, hash-addressed staging artifacts after durable archival, verify them before local cleanup, and restore them back into a local staging root without credential leakage or pretending S3 is a mounted filesystem.
acceptance: AWS dependency, credential-provider, offload, restore, checksum, collision, and documentation work stays gated behind separate approval; uploads are immutable and verified before any local delete path proceeds; restore is hash-verified and non-destructive; live S3 verification remains explicitly opt-in.
